subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Supplying the cell: diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Supplying the cell: mitosis and the cell cycle
The challenges of size: transport systems and surface area
The challenges of size: circulation, the heart and blood

questions.q: Which statement best defines diffusion?
options: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration
The movement of water across a partially permeable membrane
The movement of particles against a concentration gradient using energy
The active pumping of ions into a cell by proteins
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net, passive movement of particles down a concentration gradient from high to low concentration.

questions.q: Osmosis is best described as the movement of water molecules from a
options: dilute solution to a concentrated solution across a partially permeable membrane
concentrated solution to a dilute solution across a partially permeable membrane
high to low pressure region using energy from respiration
region of low water concentration to high water concentration
questions.explain: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane from a dilute (high water concentration) to a concentrated (low water concentration) solution.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes active transport from diffusion?
options: It requires energy from respiration and can move substances against a concentration gradient
It only moves water molecules across membranes
It moves particles down a concentration gradient without energy
It cannot move substances into cells
questions.explain: Active transport uses energy released by respiration to move substances against (up) their concentration gradient.

questions.q: Root hair cells absorb mineral ions from soil where ion concentration is lower than inside the cell. This uptake occurs by
options: active transport
osmosis
diffusion
evaporation
questions.explain: Because ions move against their concentration gradient, root hair cells must use active transport, which requires energy.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of diffusion across a cell membrane?
options: Increasing the concentration gradient
Decreasing the surface area
Increasing the diffusion distance
Lowering the temperature
questions.explain: A steeper concentration gradient increases the rate of diffusion, as do a larger surface area, a shorter distance and a higher temperature.

questions.q: A piece of potato is placed in a concentrated salt solution. After 30 minutes, what is the most likely result?
options: The potato loses mass because water leaves the cells by osmosis
The potato gains mass because water enters the cells by osmosis
The potato mass stays the same because no water moves
The potato gains mass because salt enters the cells by diffusion
questions.explain: The salt solution is more concentrated than the cell contents, so water moves out of the cells by osmosis and the potato loses mass.

questions.q: Why does active transport require energy but diffusion does not?
options: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient
Active transport only occurs in dead cells
Diffusion moves substances up the concentration gradient
Diffusion always needs a partially permeable membrane
questions.explain: Moving particles against (up) a concentration gradient is not spontaneous, so energy from respiration is needed.

questions.q: Mitosis produces daughter cells that are
options: genetically identical to the parent cell
genetically different, with half the chromosome number
genetically identical, with half the chromosome number
genetically different from each other
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes as the parent.

questions.q: A human body cell containing 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes will each new daughter cell contain?
questions.explain: Mitosis produces genetically identical diploid cells, so each daughter cell keeps the full 46 chromosomes.

questions.q: During interphase, before mitosis takes place, the cell
options: replicates its DNA and grows, increasing its number of sub-cellular structures
splits its cytoplasm into two
separates its chromosomes to opposite poles
reduces its chromosome number by half
questions.explain: In interphase the cell grows and copies its DNA and organelles in preparation for division.

questions.q: Which of the following is a role of mitosis in a multicellular organism?
options: Growth, repair of tissues and replacement of cells
Producing gametes for sexual reproduction
Creating genetic variation between offspring
Halving the chromosome number in sex cells
questions.explain: Mitosis provides identical cells for growth, tissue repair, cell replacement and asexual reproduction.

questions.q: Compared with a large organism, a very small organism has a
options: large surface area to volume ratio, allowing exchange by diffusion
small surface area to volume ratio, so it needs a transport system
large surface area to volume ratio, so it needs a transport system
small surface area to volume ratio, allowing exchange by diffusion
questions.explain: Small organisms have a large surface area to volume ratio, so diffusion alone is fast enough to supply their cells.

questions.q: Why do large multicellular organisms need specialised transport systems?
options: Their small surface area to volume ratio means diffusion alone is too slow to supply all cells
Their large surface area to volume ratio makes diffusion too fast
They have no need to exchange substances with their surroundings
Their cells do not respire and so need no oxygen
questions.explain: A small surface area to volume ratio and long diffusion distances mean large organisms require transport systems to move substances efficiently.

questions.q: A cube-shaped cell has sides of 2 cm. What is its surface area to volume ratio?
questions.explain: Surface area = 6 x (2 x 2) = 24 cm2 and volume = 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 cm3, giving a ratio of 24:8 = 3:1.

questions.q: Which set of features makes an exchange surface, such as the alveoli, efficient?
options: Large surface area, thin walls and a good blood supply
Small surface area, thick walls and no blood supply
Large surface area, thick walls and a poor blood supply
Small surface area, thin walls and no blood supply
questions.explain: Effective exchange surfaces have a large surface area, a short diffusion distance (thin walls) and a good blood supply to maintain the concentration gradient.

questions.q: In a mammal, the double circulatory system means that blood passes through the heart
options: twice for each complete circuit of the body
once for each complete circuit of the body
only when the organism is at rest
without ever entering the lungs
questions.explain: In double circulation blood passes through the heart twice per circuit: once to the lungs and once to the rest of the body.

questions.q: The four chambers of the human heart are the
options: right and left atria and the right and left ventricles
right and left atria and the right and left valves
right and left ventricles and the aorta and vena cava
right and left capillaries and the two ventricles
questions.explain: The heart has four chambers: two upper atria and two lower ventricles.

questions.q: The wall of the left ventricle is much thicker than that of the right ventricle because it must
options: pump blood at high pressure to the whole body
pump blood only to the nearby lungs
collect blood returning from the body
prevent blood from clotting inside the heart
questions.explain: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood around the entire body, so it needs a thicker, more muscular wall to generate the higher pressure.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares arteries and veins?
options: Arteries have thick muscular walls and carry blood away from the heart, while veins have valves and carry blood to the heart
Arteries have valves and carry blood to the heart, while veins have thick walls and carry blood away from the heart
Both carry blood away from the heart at high pressure
Veins are only one cell thick to allow exchange of substances
questions.explain: Arteries carry high-pressure blood away from the heart and have thick walls; veins carry lower-pressure blood back to the heart and contain valves to prevent backflow.

questions.q: A blood vessel is one cell thick, allowing oxygen and glucose to pass easily into surrounding tissues. This vessel is a
options: capillary
artery
vein
ventricle
questions.explain: Capillaries have walls that are just one cell thick, giving a short diffusion distance for the exchange of substances with tissues.
